correctness.rationale: Under Kakutani representation, a disjoint sequence in an AM-space is pointwise disjoint in a closed sublattice of \(C(K)\). Every represented center \(w\) attains its supremum norm, so the internal metric functional \(h_w\) is negative on at most one sequence term. A pointwise limit of internal metric functionals cannot be negative on two fixed terms, which gives the d-weak liminf condition. Infinite-dimensionality supplies a nonzero disjoint positive sequence, and exact rescaling realizes arbitrary positive norm profiles. The topology inclusion follows from weak lower semicontinuity of continuous convex metric functionals; the finite-dimensional endpoint is checked explicitly in \(\ell_\infty^m\).

originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 source proves the disjoint-support mechanism only in \(C[0,1]\), and the closest public database finding extends it to full compact \(C(K)\)-spaces. A general AM-space is merely a closed sublattice of a \(C(K)\)-space, so the prior theorem is not implication-level coverage: metric functionals of the sublattice are not automatically restrictions of ambient metric functionals. The present proof handles the sublattice metric-functional boundary directly. Exact semantic and alias searches found no AM-space theorem with the same all-disjoint-sequences statement or finite/infinite topology dichotomy.
